replies.content:
Type 2 diabetes often develops slowly, and early symptoms can be mild or go unnoticed. Common signs include increased thirst, frequent urination, increased hunger, fatigue, blurred vision, slow-healing sores, and frequent infections.

Risk factors include excess weight, physical inactivity, family history, and age over 45. A healthcare provider can confirm a diagnosis with tests such as fasting blood glucose or HbA1c.

Lisinopril is an ACE inhibitor used to treat high blood pressure and heart failure. The most common side effects are a dry cough, dizziness, headache, and tiredness.

Less commonly it can raise potassium levels or cause swelling of the face, lips, or throat (angioedema), which needs immediate medical care. It should not be taken during pregnancy.

A complete blood count (CBC) is a panel that measures the main components of your blood: red blood cells, white blood cells, hemoglobin, hematocrit, and platelets.

It's often used as a general health screen and to help investigate symptoms like fatigue, infection, or unexplained bruising. Reference ranges vary by laboratory, so results should be reviewed with your clinician.

The first trimester covers weeks 1 to 12. Common experiences include nausea, fatigue, breast tenderness, and frequent urination as hormone levels rise.

Key steps during this time are starting a prenatal vitamin with folic acid, booking your first prenatal appointment, and reviewing any current medications with your provider.
